name: Russell Ebert
sanfl_stats: 392 SANFL Games • 294 Goals • 4x Magarey Medallist (1971, 1974, 1976, 1980) • 3x SANFL Premierships
crossover_stats: 25 VFL Games • 15 Goals (1979) • Commuted weekly from Adelaide to Melbourne
bio: Universally revered as South Australia's greatest ever footballer. Ebert possessed peerless field vision, legendary strength, and precision handball. In 1979 he famously flew across every weekend to play for Ron Barassi's Kangaroos, still winning North Melbourne's best first-year player award.
trivia: The only player in SANFL history to win four Magarey Medals. A bronze statue of his iconic handball action stands proudly at the Eastern Gate of Adelaide Oval.

name: Malcolm Blight
sanfl_stats: 163 SANFL Games • 359 Goals • 1972 Magarey Medal • 1985 Ken Farmer Medal (126 goals)
crossover_stats: 178 VFL Games • 444 Goals • 1978 Brownlow Medal • 2x Premierships (1975, 1977)
bio: One of football's most electrifying showmen. Blight was an extraordinary high-flying forward with a booming drop punt. After dominating for Woodville and winning the 1972 Magarey, he starred at Arden St, famously kicking an after-the-siren 80-metre torpedo punt at Waverley Park in 1976.
trivia: One of only five players in football history to win both the Brownlow Medal and the Magarey Medal. Later coached the Adelaide Crows to back-to-back AFL flags in 1997 and 1998.

name: Barrie Robran
sanfl_stats: 201 SANFL Games • 257 Goals • 3x Magarey Medallist (1968, 1970, 1973) • 2x Premierships (1971, 1972)
crossover_stats: Defeated Carlton at Adelaide Oval (1972) • 17 State Games for South Australia
bio: Arguably the most graceful and complete player to grace Australian rules. Recruited from Whyalla, Robran could dominate any position from centre half-back to full-forward with balance, evasive agility, and superhuman ball control. Repeatedly turned down massive VFL offers to remain a loyal Roosters icon.
trivia: Named in the AFL Team of the Century and elevated to Legend status in the Australian Football Hall of Fame without ever playing a single VFL/AFL match.

name: Brian Leys
sanfl_stats: 91 SANFL Games • 4x SANFL Premierships (1995, 1996, 1998, 1999)
crossover_stats: 110 VFL/AFL Games • 19 Goals (1988–1994)
bio: Tough, versatile 194 cm defender and utility from Trafalgar in Gippsland who played 110 games at Punt Road before heading to Alberton in 1995. Leys became a cornerstone of Port Adelaide's dominant late-1990s era, winning four SANFL flags in five seasons.
trivia: Won four SANFL premierships in five years with Port Adelaide (1995, 1996, 1998, 1999) and later returned to Alberton as General Manager in 2012–2013.

name: Peter Maynard
sanfl_stats: 196 SANFL Games for Glenelg (1982–1990) • 2x Premierships (1985, 1986) • WWT Eagles (1991)
crossover_stats: 8 VFL Games • 5 Goals (1980–1981) • 225 Total Senior Games
bio: Dashing, courageous wingman who played eight VFL games with Melbourne before joining Glenelg in 1982 and starring in the Tigers' back-to-back 1985 and 1986 flags. He closed out his career in 1991 with the newly merged Woodville-West Torrens Eagles.
trivia: Served as the Adelaide Crows' long-time team runner and is the father of Collingwood premiership defender Brayden Maynard and former Demon Corey Maynard.

name: Bruce Winter
sanfl_stats: 296 SANFL Games • 120 Goals • 1974 & 1976 Premierships (Sturt) • 1982 & 1984 Premierships (Norwood)
crossover_stats: 12 State Games for South Australia • Fos Williams Medallist (1984)
bio: Imposing, razor-sharp defender who mastered the art of defensive organization under Jack Oatey at Unley and later Bob Hammond at The Parade. Blessed with supreme overhead marking and laser disposal out of the back half.
trivia: One of a select few players to win multiple premierships at two fierce traditional rivals (Sturt in 1974/1976 and Norwood in 1982/1984).

name: Craig Balme
sanfl_stats: 254 SANFL Games • 87 Goals • 1984 SANFL Premiership • NFC Life Member
crossover_stats: 3 VFL Games (Richmond 1983) • Brother of Norwood dual-flag coach Neil Balme
bio: Imposing full-back and ruckman who joined brother Neil Balme at The Parade in 1984, playing full-back in Norwood's famous 'History Makers' premiership from fifth place. Went on to play 254 games and earn Player Life Membership at the Redlegs.
trivia: Part of a famous WA/SA football family alongside brother Neil Balme (Subiaco/Richmond player and dual Norwood premiership coach).

name: Rick Davies
sanfl_stats: 350 SANFL Games • 671 Goals • 1976 Magarey Medal • 1974 & 1976 Flags • 1983 Ken Farmer Medal (151 goals)
crossover_stats: 20 VFL Games • 37 Goals (1981)
bio: A true giant of South Australian football. Recruited from the Mid North, Davies revolutionized the ruck position with his enormous frame, deft palming, and ground-level agility under Jack Oatey. In 1983 he went forward for South Adelaide and kicked an astonishing 151 goals in a single season.
trivia: Kicked 151 goals in the 1983 SANFL season — an all-time club record for South Adelaide that still stands today. Known universally as 'Jumbo' for his towering physical presence.

name: Stephen Copping
sanfl_stats: 246 SANFL Games • 460 Goals • 3x Glenelg Best & Fairest
crossover_stats: 42 VFL Games • 86 Goals (1982–1984)
bio: Elusive, laser-accurate goal-kicking half-forward who gave defenders nightmares with his ghostly leads and freakish goal sense. Played under Kevin Sheedy at Windy Hill in the early 1980s before returning to the Bay to terrorize SANFL backlines.
trivia: Earned the nickname 'Spook' because defenders said he would ghost into space unnoticed and snap impossible goals from tight boundary pockets.

name: Greg Phillips
sanfl_stats: 343 SANFL Games • 93 Goals • 8x SANFL Premierships • Port Adelaide Captain
crossover_stats: 84 VFL Games • 12 Goals (1983–1986)
bio: Immovable rock of the Port Adelaide defense and one of the most decorated players in South Australian history with an astonishing eight SANFL premiership medallions. Commuted to Victoria to anchor Collingwood's defense in the mid-1980s before returning to Alberton.
trivia: Father of AFLW superstar and dual league best-and-fairest winner Erin Phillips. Greg was inducted into the Australian Football Hall of Fame in 2020.

name: Tony McGuinness
sanfl_stats: 113 SANFL Games • 182 Goals • 1982 Magarey Medal • 2x Premierships (1985, 1986)
crossover_stats: 113 VFL/AFL Games (Footscray) • 110 AFL Games (Adelaide) • Dual All-Australian
bio: Lethal roving wizard who claimed the Magarey Medal in 1982 as a teenager before starring for Footscray and becoming an inaugural leader and second captain of the Adelaide Crows in the AFL.
trivia: Won the 1982 Magarey Medal at just 19 years of age. Captained the Adelaide Crows from 1995 to 1996 and won their Club Champion award in 1993.

name: Stephen Kernahan
sanfl_stats: 136 SANFL Games • 290 Goals • 1985 SANFL Premiership (Captain) • Jack Oatey Medallist
crossover_stats: 251 AFL Games • 738 Goals • 2x AFL Premiership Captain (1987, 1995) • 3x Carlton B&F
bio: One of the greatest captains and contested marks in the history of Australian football. Captained Glenelg to the famous 1985 flag at Football Park, kicking six goals in the Grand Final, before moving to Carlton where he became the longest-serving captain in VFL/AFL history.
trivia: Captained Carlton in 226 games — an AFL record for the longest captaincy tenure. Inducted into the Australian Football Hall of Fame as a true legend of the game.

name: Mark Mickan
sanfl_stats: 178 SANFL Games • 1983 SANFL Premiership • 2x West Adelaide Best & Fairest
crossover_stats: 48 Games (Brisbane Bears Inaugural Captain) • 37 Games (Adelaide Crows)
bio: Towering, athletic tap ruckman from the Barossa Valley who played a pivotal role in West Adelaide's 1983 premiership under Neil Kerley. Became the inaugural captain of the Brisbane Bears in 1987 and later joined the Adelaide Crows for their early AFL campaigns.
trivia: Won the inaugural Best and Fairest award for the Brisbane Bears in 1987 while serving as their first-ever club captain.

name: Neville Roberts
sanfl_stats: 287 SANFL Games • 676 Goals • 2x Premierships (1982, 1984) • 1982 Jack Oatey Medallist
crossover_stats: 48 VFL Games • 81 Goals (1975–1978)
bio: Deadly, theatrical full-forward who earned his haunting nickname from his uncanny ability to glide unseen behind opposition full-backs and snatch spectacular overhead marks. Booted six goals in the 1982 Grand Final to lead Norwood to premiership glory.
trivia: Kicked over 100 goals in multiple SANFL seasons for Norwood, famously wearing long sleeves even in scorching Adelaide heat.

name: Ken Farmer
sanfl_stats: 224 SANFL Games • 1,417 Goals • 11 Consecutive 100-goal seasons (1930–1940) • 2 Flags
crossover_stats: Kicked 105 goals in 17 state games for South Australia • Record 6.33 goals per game
bio: The most prolific goal kicker in the entire history of elite Australian rules football. Farmer averaged a mind-boggling 6.33 goals per match across his 13-year career at Prospect, never kicking fewer than 100 goals in any full season he played.
trivia: The SANFL leading goal kicker medal is named the 'Ken Farmer Medal' in his honour. His 1,417 career goals is an all-time elite Australian rules record.

name: Fos Williams
sanfl_stats: 151 SANFL Games • 240 Goals • 9x Premiership Coach (6 in a row: 1954–1959)
crossover_stats: Coached SA in 45 state games • Author of the famous Port Adelaide 'Creed'
bio: The legendary patriarch who forged Port Adelaide's modern powerhouse identity. Williams authored the famous Port Adelaide Club Creed in 1962 and led the Magpies to nine SANFL premierships as coach, including an Australian record six consecutive flags between 1954 and 1959.
trivia: Father of AFL premiership coach Mark Williams, SANFL premiership star Anthony Williams, and Stephen Williams. The SANFL State of Origin medal is named the Fos Williams Medal.

name: Brenton Phillips
sanfl_stats: 222 SANFL Games • 139 Goals • 1993 Magarey Medallist • 2x North Adelaide B&F
crossover_stats: 10 VFL Games (Essendon 1986) • 61 Games, 30 Goals (Brisbane Bears 1987–1991)
bio: Silky-skilled, tireless rover recruited from Gepps Cross who starred across two stints at Prospect Oval. After a brief spell at Windy Hill under Kevin Sheedy, Phillips joined the inaugural Brisbane Bears squad before returning home to claim the 1993 Magarey Medal.
trivia: Kicked the very first goal in Brisbane Bears club history in Round 1, 1987, and later coached Sturt to their drought-breaking 2002 SANFL premiership.

name: Wayne Slattery
sanfl_club: South Adelaide Panthers / North Adelaide Roosters
sanfl_stats: 189 SANFL Games (170 South, 19 North) • 249 Goals • 1987 SANFL Premiership (North Adelaide)
crossover_stats: 11 VFL Games • 12 Goals (1982)
bio: Pacy, elusive forward pocket and rover who burst onto the SANFL scene as a 16-year-old prodigy for South Adelaide. Spent 1982 at Moorabbin with St Kilda before returning to Adelaide and capping his career in North Adelaide's 1987 flag.
trivia: Debuted for the Panthers at just 16 years old in 1977 and played in the 1979 SANFL Grand Final. Father of former Essendon defender Tyson Slattery.

name: Tony Antrobus
sanfl_stats: 82 SANFL Games • 155 Goals • 1983 Magarey Medallist
crossover_stats: 28 VFL/AFL Games (22 Essendon, 6 St Kilda) • 31 Goals
bio: Pound-for-pound one of the fiercest, most explosive rovers to pull on the red-and-white V. Built low to the ground with a hair-trigger competitive streak, he tore the 1983 SANFL season apart to win the Magarey Medal at just 21, earning a move to Kevin Sheedy's Bombers before injuries curtailed his VFL/AFL stint.
trivia: Won the 1983 Magarey Medal in just his third senior season at Prospect Oval.

name: Rudi Mandemaker
sanfl_stats: 141 SANFL Games • 475 Goals • 1989 SANFL Leading Goalkicker (93 goals) • 1989 Mark of the Year
crossover_club: Hawthorn (VFL Reserves) / Adelaide Crows (1991 Inaugural Squad)
crossover_stats: Traded from Hawthorn in the John Platten deal
bio: The quintessential late-80s Elizabeth cult hero with the flowing mullet and massive leap. Recruited from Hawthorn's reserves as part of the blockbuster deal that sent John Platten to Glenferrie, Mandemaker became the focal point of Central's forward line. In 1989 he kicked 93 goals to top the SANFL goalkicking and took a trademark hanger that won Mark of the Year.
trivia: Named in the inaugural 1991 Adelaide Crows training squad after dominating the SANFL forward 50 for the Bulldogs.

name: Robbert Klomp
sanfl_stats: 205 SANFL Games • 173 Goals • 2x Premierships (1974, 1976)
crossover_stats: 93 VFL Games (84 Carlton, 9 Footscray) • 20 Goals • 2x VFL Premierships (1979, 1982) • 7 SA State Games
bio: A smooth-moving, high-leaping half-back flanker who looked like he was gliding across Unley Oval. After winning two SANFL flags with Sturt under Jack Oatey, he headed to Princes Park and became a dual VFL premiership defender under Alex Jesaulenko and David Parkin before returning to finish where he started at Unley.
trivia: Nicknamed 'Clippity' for his effortless, loping stride off half-back across both the SANFL and VFL.

name: David Hutton
sanfl_stats: 159 SANFL Games • 89 Goals • 5x SANFL Premierships (1988, 1989, 1990, 1992, 1994)
crossover_stats: 5 Grand Final Victories at Alberton
bio: The ultimate John Cahill-era utility—hard-nosed, unglamorous, and almost impossible to leave out on Grand Final day. While flashier names grabbed the headlines at Alberton, Hutton quietly stacked up five SANFL premiership medallions across the Magpies' late-80s and early-90s dynasty.
trivia: Played in five winning SANFL Grand Finals in a seven-year span for Port Adelaide.

name: Trevor Sorrell
sanfl_club: South Adelaide Panthers / North Adelaide Roosters
sanfl_stats: 245 SANFL Games (200 South Adelaide, 45 North Adelaide) • 1982 South Adelaide Best & Fairest
crossover_stats: 1987 SANFL Premiership (North Adelaide) • 200-Game Panthers Life Member
bio: With his towering frame, wild curly hair, and unmistakable presence around the stoppages at Hickinbotham/Adelaide Oval, Trevor 'Bubbles' Sorrell was pure 1980s SANFL theatre. After 200 gritty games carrying the ruck division for South Adelaide, he crossed to Prospect late in his career and finally captured an elusive SANFL premiership medallion in North Adelaide's dominant 1987 triumph.
trivia: Played exactly 200 SANFL games for South Adelaide before winning a flag with North Adelaide in his final season.

name: Danny Hughes
sanfl_stats: 117 SANFL Games • 1981 SANFL Premiership
crossover_stats: 141 VFL/AFL Games (124 Melbourne, 17 Adelaide) • 25 Goals • 6 SA State Games
bio: A fearless, no-frills full-back forged at Alberton who made a career out of spoiling the biggest forwards in both leagues. After breaking into Port Adelaide's 1981 premiership side as a teenager, Hughes became the defensive anchor of Melbourne's late-80s resurgence—playing in the 1988 VFL Grand Final—before returning home in 1991 as an inaugural Adelaide Crow.
trivia: Played in Adelaide's historic Round 1 AFL victory over Hawthorn at Football Park in 1991.

name: Bruce Lindner
sanfl_stats: 141 SANFL Games • 229 Goals • 1983 SANFL Premiership
crossover_stats: 85 VFL/AFL Games (66 Geelong, 19 Adelaide) • 119 Goals • 7 SA State Games
bio: Flamboyant, bleach-blonde, and capable of turning a game in ten minutes of pure audacity, Bruce 'Hollywood' Lindner was box-office gold in the 1980s. He starred in West Adelaide's drought-breaking 1983 premiership, lit up Kardinia Park alongside Gary Ablett Sr—including a haul of 7 goals in the 1989 Preliminary Final—and returned to kick goals in the Crows' inaugural 1991 season.
trivia: Kicked 7 goals for Geelong in the 1989 VFL Preliminary Final against Essendon.

name: Kym Hodgeman
sanfl_stats: 169 SANFL Games • 266 Goals • 1978 Glenelg Best & Fairest
crossover_stats: 96 VFL Games • 117 Goals • 11 SA State Games
bio: A silky, elusive left-footer with lethal goal sense and a wicked sidestep, Kym Hodgeman was a fixture of Glenelg's powerhouse mid-70s teams before heading to Arden Street. Under Ron Barassi and Barry Cable at North Melbourne, he proved small South Australian rovers could thrive in heavy Victorian mud, representing South Australia 11 times in State of Origin.
trivia: Won Glenelg's Best & Fairest in 1978 and represented South Australia 11 times.

name: Michael Taylor
sanfl_stats: 289 SANFL Games • 166 Goals • 4x SANFL Premierships (1975, 1978, 1982, 1984)
crossover_stats: 94 VFL Games • 36 Goals • 11 SA State Games • 4x Norwood Best & Fairest
bio: One of Norwood's most decorated modern warriors, Michael Taylor combined tireless engine-room work with crunching tackling across two eras at The Parade. Bookending a gritty 94-game VFL stint at Collingwood with four Redlegs flags and four club Best & Fairest awards, he captained Norwood's famous 'History Makers' premiership from fifth place in 1984.
trivia: Captained Norwood from 5th on the ladder to win the famous 1984 SANFL Grand Final.

name: Bruce Abernethy
sanfl_stats: 190 SANFL Games • 115 Goals • 7x SANFL Premierships (1979, 1980, 1981, 1988, 1989, 1990, 1992) • 1988 Jack Oatey Medallist
crossover_club: North Melbourne Kangaroos / Collingwood Magpies (VFL) • Adelaide Crows (AFL)
crossover_stats: 112 VFL/AFL Games (43 North Melbourne, 58 Collingwood, 11 Adelaide) • 39 Goals • 10 SA State Games
bio: A silky, running wingman and half-back flanker who collected premierships at Alberton like confetti while also logging over a century of VFL/AFL matches across North Melbourne, Collingwood, and the inaugural Adelaide Crows. He won Port Adelaide's Best & Fairest in 1987 and claimed the 1988 Jack Oatey Medal before health issues forced an early retirement.
trivia: Won seven SANFL premierships with Port Adelaide, capping his career with a flag in 1992 after playing 11 AFL games for the Crows.

name: Greg Whittlesea
sanfl_stats: 255 SANFL Games • 89 Goals • 1988 Magarey Medallist • Sturt Captain (1987–1990)
crossover_stats: 4 AFL Games (1991) • 2x Sturt Best & Fairest (1987, 1988) • 1988 All-Australian
bio: A gritty, dependable on-baller who carried Sturt through tough late-80s seasons as club captain from 1987 to 1990. Whittlesea peaked in 1988 with back-to-back Sturt Best & Fairest awards, All-Australian honours at the Bicentennial Carnival, and the Magarey Medal, before a brief stint at Hawthorn and a long second act at Yankalilla.
trivia: After his SANFL and AFL days, he played 168 games for Yankalilla in South Australia's Great Southern Football League.

name: Gilbert McAdam
sanfl_stats: 86 SANFL Games • 92 Goals (1988–1990, 1998) • 1989 Magarey Medallist
crossover_stats: 111 AFL Games (53 St Kilda, 58 Brisbane Bears) • 89 Goals
bio: Electrifying, mercurial, and capable of the impossible around goal, Gilbert McAdam made history in 1989 by winning the SANFL Magarey Medal with Central District—becoming the first Indigenous player to claim the award. He went on to light up Moorabbin with St Kilda and play 58 games for the Brisbane Bears before returning to Elizabeth.
trivia: Won the 1989 Magarey Medal for Central District, becoming the first Indigenous player to win the SANFL's highest individual honour.

name: Paul Weston
sanfl_club: Glenelg Tigers / West Torrens Eagles / Norwood Redlegs
sanfl_stats: 268 SANFL Games (196 Glenelg, 49 West Torrens, 23 Norwood) • 205 Goals
crossover_stats: 60 VFL Games • 12 Goals (1983–1985) • 328 Total Senior Games, 217 Goals
bio: A durable, smart-moving left-footed midfielder who racked up 328 senior appearances across the SANFL and VFL. After logging nearly 200 games for Glenelg and three seasons at Essendon in the mid-80s, he wound out his career with stints at West Torrens and Norwood.
trivia: Played across three SANFL clubs—Glenelg, West Torrens, and Norwood—alongside 60 VFL games for Essendon.

name: Peter Woite
sanfl_stats: 202 SANFL Games (182 Port Adelaide, 20 Glenelg) • 141 Goals • 1975 Magarey Medallist
crossover_stats: 1977 SANFL Premiership (Port Adelaide) • 1975 Port Best & Fairest • 12 SA State Games
bio: Classy, composed, and lethal with the ball in hand, Peter Woite was a mainstay of Port Adelaide through the 1970s. He swept the 1975 Magarey Medal and Port Adelaide Best & Fairest, played in Port's 1977 premiership, and finished his career with two seasons at Glenelg to pass 200 SANFL games.
trivia: Won the 1975 Magarey Medal at Port Adelaide and played in their 1977 SANFL premiership side.

name: Greg Anderson
sanfl_club: Port Adelaide Magpies / South Adelaide Panthers
sanfl_stats: 80 SANFL Games (59 Port Adelaide, 21 South Adelaide) • 67 Goals • 1986 Magarey Medallist
crossover_stats: 159 VFL/AFL Games (103 Essendon, 56 Adelaide) • 79 Goals • 1989 Essendon Best & Fairest
bio: A silky, running wingman with effortless pace and disposal off either foot, Greg Anderson won the 1986 Magarey Medal at Port Adelaide before crossing to Kevin Sheedy's Essendon. He claimed the Crichton Medal as Essendon's Best & Fairest in 1989 and played in the 1990 VFL/AFL Grand Final before returning home to play 56 AFL games for the Adelaide Crows.
trivia: Won both the SANFL Magarey Medal (1986) and Essendon's Best & Fairest (1989).

name: Mark Naley
sanfl_stats: 216 SANFL Games • 183 Goals • 1991 Magarey Medallist • 2x South Adelaide Best & Fairest (1984, 1991)
crossover_stats: 65 VFL/AFL Games • 74 Goals • 1987 VFL Premiership • 1987 Fos Williams Medallist
bio: Small in stature but fearless at every contest, Mark Naley was a South Adelaide icon who proved elite SA rovers could conquer Melbourne. After starring for South Adelaide, he crossed to Carlton and played a starring role in the Blues' 1987 VFL Grand Final triumph, before returning to Noarlunga to win the 1991 Magarey Medal.
trivia: Won the 1987 VFL Premiership with Carlton and the 1987 Fos Williams Medal for South Australia before winning the 1991 Magarey Medal.

name: Garry McIntosh
sanfl_stats: 371 SANFL Games • 193 Goals • 2x Magarey Medallist (1994, 1995) • 2x SANFL Premierships (1984, 1997)
crossover_stats: 2x Jack Oatey Medallist (1984, 1997) • 6x Norwood Best & Fairest • 13 SA State Games
bio: Ferocious, uncompromising, and fiercely loyal to The Parade, Garry McIntosh famously resisted repeated AFL overtures to become one of the greatest one-club warriors in SANFL history. Over 371 games for Norwood, he won two Magarey Medals, six club Best & Fairest awards, and two Jack Oatey Medals 13 years apart in the Redlegs' 1984 and 1997 flags.
trivia: Won the Jack Oatey Medal as best afield in both the 1984 and 1997 SANFL Grand Finals—13 years apart.

name: Ray Huppatz
sanfl_stats: 169 SANFL Games • 111 Goals • 4x Woodville Best & Fairest
crossover_stats: 117 VFL Games (90 Footscray, 27 North Melbourne) • 79 Goals • 8 SA State Games
bio: Elusive, balanced, and blessed with razor-sharp foot skills, Ray Huppatz was Woodville's brightest star during the Warriors' battling early SANFL years. Winning four club Best & Fairest awards at Oval Avenue, he crossed to Victoria in 1973 and played 117 VFL games across Footscray and North Melbourne—including the Kangaroos' 1978 Grand Final—before returning to Woodville.
trivia: Won four Woodville Best & Fairest awards and played 286 combined senior SANFL and VFL matches.

name: Martin Leslie
sanfl_stats: 153 SANFL Games • 14 Goals • 2x SANFL Premierships (1981, 1988) • 1983 Port Adelaide Best & Fairest
crossover_stats: 107 VFL/AFL Games • 8 Goals • 1989 Brisbane Bears Best & Fairest • 8 SA State Games
bio: A granite-jawed, uncompromising full-back forged at Alberton under John Cahill, Martin Leslie made life miserable for spearheads in both South Australia and Queensland. After winning two SANFL flags with Port Adelaide, he became a cornerstone of the fledgling Brisbane Bears defence, winning their 1989 Best & Fairest and passing 100 AFL games.
trivia: Won Port Adelaide's Best & Fairest in 1983 and the Brisbane Bears' Best & Fairest in 1989.

name: Richard Champion
sanfl_stats: 91 SANFL Games • 1990 Woodville Best & Fairest
crossover_stats: 183 AFL Games • 26 Goals • Brisbane Lions Life Member
bio: Curly-haired, hard-at-it, and impossible to miss on the field or behind a microphone, Richard Champion won Woodville's final Best & Fairest award in 1990 before the club merged into the Eagles. Drafted to Queensland, he became a beloved 183-game cult hero across the Brisbane Bears and merged Brisbane Lions eras.
trivia: Won Woodville's final Best & Fairest medal in 1990 before playing 183 AFL games for Brisbane.
